Is KuCoin Safe in 2026? What the Controversy Means for Traders

Guides · 7 min read · Updated June 2026

KuCoin spent years as a go-to venue for altcoins and futures. In 2026 it is more of a cautionary tale. If you are asking whether KuCoin is safe to trade on, the honest answer is: it still works, but it carries more trust baggage than almost any other major exchange — and trust is the one factor that outweighs fees, leverage and everything else. Here is the sourced picture, framed as public reporting, so you can decide for yourself. Not financial advice.

The US guilty plea (January 2025)

KuCoin pleaded guilty in the United States to operating an unlicensed money-transmitting business, agreeing to roughly $300 million in penalties and forfeitures. Prosecutors said prior anti-money-laundering and know-your-customer failures let suspicious funds move through the platform. KuCoin is banned for US users as a result. A guilty plea from a top-tier exchange is not a small footnote — it tells you how regulators viewed its controls.

The ZachXBT allegations (2026)

On-chain investigator ZachXBT — one of the most credible independent researchers in crypto — turned repeated attention to KuCoin in 2026. He asked the exchange to explain how roughly $9.5 million stolen via a fake Ledger app was laundered through more than 150 KuCoin deposit addresses in a single week, and later wrote that the exchange "does not assist victims or law enforcement," calling the team "complicit" and alleging that illicit funds move freely so long as they generate fees. In a separate case, a user who lost $250,000 to a wallet theft said the funds landed in KuCoin addresses allegedly opened with purchased "mule" KYC — and that when a community member spoke out, KuCoin reportedly threatened legal action over "false or unlawful statements." KuCoin disputes these characterizations; treat them as reporting and verify the current facts yourself.

The EU restriction (February 2026)

Austria's financial regulator, the FMA, barred KuCoin's EU arm from onboarding new customers after it reportedly lost its key anti-money-laundering and sanctions compliance officers. Losing compliance leadership and an onboarding ban in a major jurisdiction is a serious operational red flag on its own.

What "safe" actually means for a trader

An exchange can have great fees and deep liquidity and still be unsafe, because the only question that matters when things go wrong is: can you get your money out? The signals that answer it are regulation, security record, proof of reserves, and — underrated until you need it — how the venue treats victims and investigators. On those measures, KuCoin now rates poorly. None of this guarantees the exchange fails tomorrow, but the combination of a guilty plea, an EU onboarding ban, unpaid court awards and repeated victim-handling accusations is precisely the backdrop that has tended to precede withdrawal problems elsewhere.

The practical verdict

If you choose to use KuCoin, the cautious playbook is simple: keep minimal balances, withdraw profits promptly, and never treat it as custody. Better still, prefer a venue with a cleaner record.
